correction.text: the 1945 outline Cliopatria files under its 'Yugoslavia' row (250,300 km2), which is the territory of the Federal People's Republic proclaimed on 29 November 1945; unchanged in shape, the row only changes hands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, shape unchanged: Cliopatria's 'Socialist Federal Republic' row starts in 1946, but the page says 'on 29 November 1945, the Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia was proclaimed' (the infobox also gives 31 January 1946 as 'FPR Yugoslavia proclaimed'). The Kingdom of Yugoslavia row (slug yugoslavia) holds the 1945 shape; the two dossiers should split the year, this one from November.

250,843 km2 against the infobox's 255,804 km2 (ratio 0.98; the infobox gives no year). The shape already holds Istria, the Fiume coast and Zara, which were Yugoslav-held in 1946 and formally ceded only when the treaty took effect on 15 September 1947 (ledger 1945-11 to 1947-09). The 1946 outline differs from 1947 by two grid cells at the Hungarian frontier, which is drawing noise.

250,634 km2: the outline of the Paris peace treaty. Signed 10 February 1947 and effective 15 September 1947, it ceded 'Istria, the provinces of Fiume, Zara, and most of Gorizia and Pola' to Yugoslavia and created the Free Territory of Trieste, whose Zone B Yugoslav troops held; the shape holds two cells (about 506 km2) at Trieste/Koper, matching Zone B's 515.5 km2. The page reports no border move in 1948 (the Tito-Stalin split, 'in the spring and early summer of 1948').

250,252 km2, constant to 1990: the London Memorandum of 5 October 1954 left Zone A to Italy and Zone B to Yugoslavia, which the shape already shows, and the Treaty of Osimo 'formalized' the line (ratified 1977). The 1949 outline lacks two cells on the Greek frontier that the 1947 shape had (about 506 km2, drawing noise, no event).

250,252 km2, the whole federation; the page dates the secession of Slovenia and Croatia to 25 June 1991, Macedonia's declaration to 25 September 1991 and Bosnia's to 3 March 1992, with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia proclaimed in April 1992. Cliopatria draws the successors from 1992, so the shape stands to the end of 1991; the Slovenian and Croatian fronts are contest events.

region.text: the Julian March east of the Morgan Line, 'their area' to which the Yugoslav troops withdrew on 12 June 1945: Istria, the Fiume (Rijeka) coast and the Gorizia lands east of the line; the page names the line and 'their area', not the places, so the provinces are the researcher's reading

ledger.note: 1945: the Julian March east of the Morgan Line is under Yugoslav military administration when the Federal People's Republic is proclaimed on 29 November 1945; the occupation is opened at the founding month because the state did not exist earlier, and it is inherited from the Yugoslav army's administration since May-June 1945. The page: Yugoslav units 'entered Trieste on 1 May 1945'; 'A formal agreement on partition was signed in Duino on 10 June' (the Morgan Line); 'Yugoslav troops withdrew to their area on 12 June 1945'; Dusan Kveder is listed as Yugoslav governor from 1 May 1945 to September 1947. The owner is the Kingdom of Italy, which lasts to June 1946; the occupation continues under the Republic in the next two events (one counterpart string per pair). The region is the researcher's reading of 'their area'.

'Istria, the provinces of Fiume, Zara, and most of Gorizia and Pola were ceded to Yugoslavia'; the treaties 'were signed on 10 February 1947' and took effect on 15 September 1947. region.text: Zone B, '515.5 square kilometres ... with 71,000 residents', administered by the Yugoslav army: the north-western corner of Istria, named here as the Koper, Izola and Piran municipalities and a 22 km circle on Umag, Buje and Novigrad (the same reading as the Free Territory of Trieste dossier)

ledger.note: 1947: Zone B of the Free Territory of Trieste is run by the Yugoslav army. The Free Territory 'came into existence on 15 September 1947'; 'Zone B ... 515.5 square kilometres with 71,000 residents' was administered by the Yugoslav army, Zone A by British and American forces.

region.text: Zone B, '515.5 square kilometres ... with 71,000 residents', administered by the Yugoslav army: the north-western corner of Istria, named here as the Koper, Izola and Piran municipalities and a 22 km circle on Umag, Buje and Novigrad (the same reading as the Free Territory of Trieste dossier)

ledger.note: 1954: the Free Territory ends as the London Memorandum, signed on 5 October 1954, shares it out; Zone B stays with Yugoslavia and Italian troops take over Zone A on 25 October.

region.text: Zone B, '515.5 square kilometres ... with 71,000 residents', administered by the Yugoslav army: the north-western corner of Istria, named here as the Koper, Izola and Piran municipalities and a 22 km circle on Umag, Buje and Novigrad (the same reading as the Free Territory of Trieste dossier)

ledger.note: 1954: Zone B passes to Yugoslavia. The London Memorandum was signed 'on 5 October 1954' and provided that Zone B 'would be annexed by Yugoslavia'; 'the new borders were formalized twenty-one years later by the Treaty of Osimo' (1975, ratified 1977), which moves no line. Nine villages of Zone A that also went to Yugoslavia are in the Free Territory dossier, not on this page.

1963: the Federal People's Republic becomes the Socialist Federal Republic. 'In 1963, amid pervasive liberal constitutional reforms, the name Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was introduced.' Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Slovenia, where 'the short armed conflict' of June and July 1991 was fought

ledger.note: 1991: the Yugoslav army fights Slovenia after its declaration of 25 June. The Ten-Day War page: infobox '27 June - 7 July 1991'; 'It lasted from 27 June 1991 until 7 July 1991, when the Brioni Accords were signed.' Slovenia and Croatia 'declared their independence on 25 June 1991' (Breakup page).

1991: the Brioni Agreement of 7 July 1991 ends the fighting in Slovenia ('when the Brioni Accords were signed'; 'Slovenia and Croatia would postpone their independence for three months'). The army's withdrawal 'began about ten days later and was completed by 26 October' 1991. Slovenia is drawn Yugoslav to the end of 1991 and passes to the Republic of Slovenia with the dissolution.

region.text: the Croatian land outside Zagreb's control in 1992-1995 (Cliopatria's Croatia of 1996 minus its Croatia of 1992, about 12,900 km2): the Krajina and Slavonian lands that 'the Yugoslav army and other Serb forces' held, 'something less than one-third of the Croatian territory' a month after 25 June 1991

ledger.note: 1991: the army and Serb forces hold a third of Croatia and press on Vukovar. 'In August 1991, the Battle of Vukovar began' and a month after 25 June 'the Yugoslav army and other Serb forces held something less than one-third of the Croatian territory'. The war had begun with the Plitvice Lakes incident of 'late March 1991'; the zone is Cliopatria's 1992-1995 gap in Croatia, a reading.

region.text: the Croatian land outside Zagreb's control in 1992-1995 (Cliopatria's Croatia of 1996 minus its Croatia of 1992, about 12,900 km2): the Krajina and Slavonian lands that 'the Yugoslav army and other Serb forces' held, 'something less than one-third of the Croatian territory' a month after 25 June 1991

ledger.note: 1991: the federation ceases to be a party to the Croatian front when it is declared dissolving. No page dates an end to the army's own front inside 1991: the Commission replied on 29 November 1991 that 'the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia is in the process of dissolution' (Badinter page), and the Croatian War page dates the UN-sponsored ceasefire to 2 January 1992 ('agreed on January 2, 1992, and came into force the next day'), after which the JNA 'soon retreated from Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina'. This dossier ends in 1991, so the contest is closed in November, between those two dated anchors (confidence 1, a bridge). The fighting went on between Croatia and the Serb entity (republic-of-serbian-krajina) after the SFRY's end, and Cliopatria draws the Serb-held land under Serbia-Montenegro in 1992.

region.text: the whole federation, whose land passes to Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia

ledger.note: 1991: the federation falls apart. Slovenia and Croatia declared independence on 25 June, Macedonia on 25 September 1991 (referendum 8 September), Bosnia on 3 March 1992; the Badinter Commission replied on 29 November 1991 that the SFRY 'is in the process of dissolution' (Badinter page) and the page dates its formal break-up to 27 April 1992 (the Federal Republic proclaimed by Serbia and Montenegro). This dossier ends in 1991, as Cliopatria's row does, and the successors are drawn from 1992.

wars.outcome: Slovenia left the federation; the Brioni Agreement of 7 July 1991 imposed a three-month moratorium during which the army's withdrawal, begun about ten days later, was completed by 26 October 1991.
wars.note: Span from the Ten-Day War page: infobox '27 June - 7 July 1991' ('It lasted from 27 June 1991 until 7 July 1991, when the Brioni Accords were signed').

wars.name: Croatian War of Independence

zones.text: the Croatian land outside Zagreb's control in 1992-1995 (Cliopatria's Croatia of 1996 minus its Croatia of 1992, about 12,900 km2): the Krajina and Slavonian lands that 'the Yugoslav army and other Serb forces' held, 'something less than one-third of the Croatian territory' a month after 25 June 1991

wars.outcome: The war as a whole runs from 1 March 1991 to 12 November 1995 (infobox), but the SFRY's part ends with its dissolution in 1991 (the span here is held to the state's life). The Yugoslav army and Serb forces held something less than one-third of Croatia one month after 25 June 1991; a UN-sponsored ceasefire was agreed on 2 January 1992 and came into force the next day, and the JNA 'soon retreated from Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina'; the war ended in November 1995.
wars.note: Start: the infobox gives 1 March 1991, the text the Plitvice Lakes incident of late March 1991; the SFRY dossier opens the contest in August 1991 (Vukovar).

certainty.note: The Julian March (Morgan Line) and Trieste were provisional and in dispute; the other frontiers are those of the Kingdom.

The Italian frontier is the 1947 peace treaty's; Zone B of the Free Territory is provisional to the 1954 London Memorandum, formalised by the Treaty of Osimo (ratified 1977); the other frontiers were not examined on the pages opened.
The front lines in Croatia (the Serb-held third) and the republics' claims were moving; the Slovenian line is the republic border.

notes: One dossier for the Socialist Federal Republic (Cliopatria's 1946-1991 row). It shares Wikidata Q83286 with the Cliopatria row 'Yugoslavia' (slug yugoslavia, 1919-1945), the Kingdom of Yugoslavia: these are different states (the monarchy was replaced by the Federal People's Republic proclaimed on 29 November 1945), so they are not merged; the 1945 shape is split between them in November (new keyframe here, shape unchanged). The state ends in 1991 as Cliopatria's row does; the SFRY page dates the formal break-up to 27 April 1992 and Cliopatria draws the successors from 1992. Occupation of the Julian March and the Free Territory's Zone B follows the occupation convention (the occupier records occupation_start with the owner as counterpart). Not settled: the Dalmatian islands, Zara and the Lastovo group, which the Paris page does not name; the Tito-Stalin split of 1948, Tito's death on 4 May 1980 and the 1963 constitution date have no territorial effect and no ledger event beyond the rename. A gap-filler could open 'Treaty of Osimo' and 'Yugoslav occupation of Trieste'. Slovenia, Croatia, Macedonia and Bosnia have Cliopatria shapes only from 1992, so the 1991 losses are not ledgered as separate gains: the republic-of-slovenia, republic-of-croatia and former-yugoslav-republic-of-macedonia dossiers should start in 1991 or 1992 consistently with the dissolve here. Gazetteer names used: none missing (Koper, Izola, Piran, Istarska, Primorsko-Goranska, Nova Goriška, Zadar and Klagenfurt resolve). REPAIR PASS 2026-11-01 (reviewer verdict fail). (1) The two Carinthia events (Klagenfurt, May 1945) are removed: they precede the state's start (1945-11) and belong to the dossier of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia (slug yugoslavia, eu-21; second-republic-of-austria already names it as counterpart); the Carinthia page is no longer in sources. The alternative of starting the state in March 1945 as Democratic Federal Yugoslavia was not taken: the SFRY page's own infobox lists 'Democratic Federal Yugoslavia' as a predecessor and yugoslav-partisans/yugoslavia hand their land over, so the state starts at the proclamation of 29 November 1945. (2) The Julian March occupation is opened at 1945-11 (inherited from the Yugoslav army's administration since 1 May / 12 June 1945, both on the Free Territory page) with the Kingdom of Italy as owner, closed and reopened in June 1946 with the Italian Republic (Kingdom of Italy page: monarchy abolished 18 June 1946), and closed 1947-09; kingdom-of-italy and republic-of-italy carry no mirror 'occupied by' event (the republic-of-italy dossier records a 1947-09 loss to this state, which matches the gain). (3) The Croatian War span ends 1991 (the war's own end, 12 November 1995, is in the outcome). (4) republika-srpska (found 1992-01) and croatian-republic-of-herzeg-bosnia (found 1991-11) are added to the successors; I did not add loss events for them, because the first lies outside the dossier's years and the second is an autonomous community inside Bosnia whose land is counted again under bosnia-and-herzegovina. Thin items: the Ten-Day War page now gives 27 June to 7 July 1991 and the withdrawal completed by 26 October 1991 (events 10 and 11 raised to confidence 3); the Croatian contest_end stays at confidence 1 because no page dates the end of the army's front inside 1991: it sits between the Badinter reply of 29 November 1991 and the ceasefire of 2 January 1992, and it is sourced to the Badinter page. Four pages were opened beyond the 5-page budget (Ten-Day War and Badinter as the reviewer directed, Kingdom of Italy for the June 1946 owner change, Herzeg-Bosnia for the 18 November 1991 date). Disagreement with the reviewer: none on substance; the page-dated 2 January 1992 ceasefire was not used as the contest_end date because it lies after the dossier's end.
